A.notes: A has a clear minimal idea around flame-marked ware, but it feels closest to a polished contemporary template rather than a fully authored ceramics identity. The scroll-strip suggests a serviceable firing-story progression, yet the full-page and mobile captures show large empty spans that hurt confidence in visual craft and continuity. Accessibility and baseline implementation checks are strong.

B.notes: B turns the small-batch brief into the product concept itself: the numbered 32-piece selection grid, editorial shelf list, and kiln-story section all reinforce one idea. Typography carries the brand most strongly here, with a confident serif/sans system and much better hierarchy than A. Motion evidence is limited in the strip, so I only credit modest, concept-aligned progression rather than standout animation.

raw.why: B is the more complete and distinctive response to the brief, with a stronger concept, sharper typography, and more reliable craft while still meeting the functional checks.
